title: SYSK Selects: Juggling: What the Heck
summary: A Stuff You Should Know Selects rerun (originally aired January 2015) on juggling. The hosts cover juggling history from ancient Egypt through the Talmud, medieval jugglers, vaudeville, and the founding of juggling associations and competitions. They then walk listeners through learning toss juggling: starting with one bean bag, the cascade and reverse cascade, and tricks such as the shower, tennis move, bounce juggling, clawing, and chops. Other topics include juggling props, numbers juggling, cigar box and shaker cup juggling, contact ring juggling, passing and stealing-and-replacing, combat juggling, the physics of gravity in juggling, Shannon's juggling theorem, site swapping notation, and how jugglers track objects visually. The episode ends with a listener mail story about a listener's husband in the hospital awaiting a bone marrow transplant.

segments.title: Rerun intro and juggling banter
segments.summary: Chuck introduces the Selects rerun of the juggling episode while the hosts joke about juggling and their own attempts to learn.

segments.title: History of juggling
segments.summary: Juggling dates to ancient Egypt, with mentions of Greece, Rome, India, and a Talmudic rabbi said to juggle eight torches. Jugglers' reputation declined in Rome, rose and fell in the medieval era, then became circus and vaudeville acts. Juggling associations and championships followed in the 1940s and 1960s.

segments.title: Notable jugglers and resources
segments.summary: The hosts mention Jonathan Strickland's juggling article, instructional YouTube videos by Adam Shamsky, and Anthony Gatto's record-setting career and his retirement.

segments.title: Learning to juggle: starting with bean bags
segments.summary: Beginners should start with bean bags rather than balls, practice one-ball tossing for consistent arc, stand near a wall, and learn the scooping hand motion for the cascade.

segments.title: The cascade pattern and adding balls
segments.summary: The cascade is described as a figure-eight hand motion with alternating tosses. The hosts explain how to build from one ball to two and then three, with timing and the flash of juggling.

segments.title: Reverse cascade and juggling tricks
segments.summary: The reverse cascade reverses hand direction. The hosts describe tricks such as the half shower, tennis move, Mills mess, and bounce juggling, along with clawing and chops.

segments.title: Juggling patterns, props and bartender flair
segments.summary: Odd and even prop counts require different patterns. The hosts discuss toss juggling with one or two hands, fountain and column patterns, synchronous versus asynchronous juggling, cigar box and shaker cup juggling, and bartender flair.

segments.title: Juggling with partners and combat juggling
segments.summary: Two jugglers can pass clubs or balls, or steal and replace each other's props. The hosts describe passing patterns and combat juggling, where jugglers try to knock props from one another's hands.

segments.title: Physics and math of juggling
segments.summary: Gravity's constant acceleration means throws must go higher as props are added. Mass affects difficulty. Shannon's juggling theorem and site swapping notation are discussed, along with research on how jugglers track props visually.
